auth.title: Authenticate API requests
highlights:
A majority of Klaviyo’s APIs are server-side endpoints, which should be securely handled on your server rather than exposed in the browser. Handle sensitive information via server-side APIs, like bulk-creating events for one or more profiles.

Client-side APIs are used to track and send user behavior data from the client to Klaviyo. They are designed to be called from publicly-searchable, client-side environments only (see Client API reference).

Klaviyo provides 3 methods of authentication including private key authentication and OAuth (used to call server-side APIs) and public key authentication (used to call client-side APIs). Read the table below to learn more about how each method can be used for authenticating API calls:

| Server-side APIs |  | Client-side APIs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Private key authentication All /api endpoints use API private keys to authenticate requests. If you do not use an API key for your requests, or if you use a key from the wrong account, your call will return an error. A 400 error indicates an invalid or missing API key.  | OAuth If you are a tech partner integrating with Klaviyo, we recommend using OAuth to make authorized API calls. OAuth offers multiple benefits over a private key integration, including security, usability, improved rate limits, and the ability to be listed in Klaviyo's App Marketplace. | Public key authentication All /client endpoints use a public API key: your 6-character company ID, also known as a site ID. We recommend using the Klaviyo object or our Mobile SDKs for interacting with our client-side APIs. |

> ## 📘
> 
> To manage API keys, you must have an Owner, Admin, or Manager role on your Klaviyo account.

Private key authentication

Private API keys can be used to read and write data to your Klaviyo account. Klaviyo allows you to generate multiple private keys for your applications.

> ## 🚧
> 
> For your account's security, your private API keys should never be used with Client endpoints, exposed in client-side code, or made accessible from public repositories.

Create a private key

To create a private key:

1. Navigate to your account’s Settings page and select API keys.
2. Under the Private API Keys section, select Create Private API Key.

3. Provide a name for your private key and add any of the following scopes:

- Custom Key   Allows you to decide how much access to give the third party.
- Read-Only Key   Only allows third parties to view all data associated with the endpoint.
- Full Access Key   Allows third parties to create, delete, or make changes to anything associated with that endpoint.

> ## 🚧
> 
> Note that you cannot add a scope to an existing private key. You also cannot edit a private API key after it’s been created. If you need to remove access to a key based on its current scope, delete it and then create a new key with the correct scope.

4. When you have finished setting your key’s scopes, select Create. To protect your account from unauthorized access, you cannot view your private API keys in Klaviyo. After you have created your private API key, copy it to a secure location.

Private keys will have the prefix pk_ followed by a longer alphanumeric string.

Use a private key

Private key authentication for Copy Code `/api` endpoints is performed by setting the following request header:

```
Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key your-private-api-key

```

```curl
curl --request GET \
     --url https://a.klaviyo.com/api/{endpoint}/ \
     --header 'Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key your-private-api-key' \
     --header 'accept: application/json' \
     --header 'revision: 2026-10-15'

```

Public key authentication

Your 6-character public key, sometimes referred to as a site ID, is a short alphanumeric string that serves as the unique identifier for your Klaviyo account.

Public keys cannot be used to access secure data in your account and are safe to share. Use your public key when you need to track people and events in client-side JavaScript code.

Client-side API calls only require a public API key, also known as a Copy Code `company_id`, for authentication:

```curl
curl --request POST \
     --url 'https://a.klaviyo.com/client/subscriptions/?company_id=PUBLIC_API_KEY' \
     --header 'content-type: application/json' \
     --header 'revision: 2026-10-15' \
     --data '
     ...

```

OAuth

If you're building an app with Klaviyo, use OAuth to provide secure delegated access to users via access tokens (required to enter Klaviyo’s App Marketplace). When setting up OAuth, you must provide designated scopes for each API authorization request you'll want to make.

Set custom scopes

Setting custom scopes helps you protect your and your customers’ data by limiting what third parties can access. When requesting authorization to make API calls (OAuth), you should only request the scopes required to use your app.

View the API reference documentation to understand which scopes you’ll need to define. For example, if your private key or Klaviyo app needs to create lists, your app needs the Copy Code `lists:write` scope as shown in the following API reference documentation for the Create List endpoint:

See the full list of scopes needed for each of our APIs below:

Available scopes for each API 

 

 

| API endpoint  | Associated scopes  |
| --- | --- |
| Accounts  | `accounts:read`  |
| Campaigns  | `campaigns:read`  `campaigns:write`  |
| Conversations  | `conversations:read`  `conversations:write`  |
| Catalogs  | `catalogs:read`  `catalogs:write`  |
| Coupons  | `coupons:read`  `coupons:write`  |
| Coupon codes  | `coupon-codes:read`  `coupon-codes:write`  |
| Data privacy  | `data-privacy:read`  `data-privacy:write`  |
| Events  | `events:read`  `events:write` (allows for creating/updating profiles)  |
| Flows  | `flows:read`  `flows:write`  |
| Forms  | `forms:read`  |
| Images  | `images:read`  `images:write`  |
| Lists  | `lists:read`  `lists:write`  |
| Metrics  | `metrics:read`  `metrics:write`  |
| Profiles  | `profiles:read`  `profiles:write`  |
| Push tokens  | `push-tokens:read`  `push-tokens:write`  |
| Reporting  | `campaigns:read`  `flows:read` `forms:read`   `segments:read` |
| Reviews  | `reviews:read`   |
| Segments  | `segments:read`  `segments:write`  |
| Subscriptions  | `subscriptions:read`  `subscriptions:write`  |
| Tags  | `tags:read`  `tags:write`  |
| Templates  | `templates:read`  `templates:write`  |
| Tracking Settings  | `tracking-settings:read`  `tracking-settings:write`  |

auth.title: Make API calls using OAuth
highlights:
> ## ❗️
> 
> On March 31, 2025, Klaviyo started blocking all OAuth token traffic (Copy Code `oauth/token` and Copy Code `oauth/revoke`) routed through Copy Code `www.klaviyo.com`. Ensure that your integration routes token traffic to Copy Code `https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token` or Copy Code `https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/revoke` to avoid breakages.

Before you begin

Before you can initiate an OAuth connection, you need to create an app in Klaviyo. If each user should install and authorize your app separately, see Build a user-scoped app before you create it.

> ## 🚧
> 
> Note that only owner, admin, and manager roles can create OAuth apps in Klaviyo. Learn more about user management and privileges.

...

OAuth authorization code flow

> ## ❗️
> 
> Your app must use OAuth in order to be considered for Klaviyo’s App Marketplace.

When a Klaviyo user installs your integration, they grant your app permission to use Klaviyo’s APIs on their behalf. You will be able to authenticate these APIs using access tokens. These access tokens come from integration with Klaviyo’s authorization code flow (shown below).

Construct your app's installation URL

The installation URL initiates the OAuth authorization flow for the account. This is where users will be directed to begin the installation process of your app after they click Install on your app’s listing page.

When a user installs your app, the list of permissions they’ll see will look like this:

Redirect the user to the authorization flow by constructing the following URL:

Copy Code `https://www.klaviyo.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id={client_id}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}&scope={scopes}&state={state}&code_challenge_method=S256&code_challenge={code_challenge}`

The URL contains the following required parameters:

| Query parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Copy Code `response_type` | Set to Copy Code `code`. Represents the authorization code provided to retrieve the access token. |
| Copy Code `client_id` | The client ID of your app. |
| Copy Code `redirect_uri` | The user is redirected here after the authorization page. This must exactly match a URL that has been entered in the allowlist for your integration at https://www.klaviyo.com/manage-apps. Note that your OAuth app must be able to support installation from both klaviyo.com and any subdomain of klaviyo.com. |
| Copy Code `scope` | A space-separated list of scopes corresponding to the list of permissions that the user will be shown when they are authorizing the app. Example: Copy Code `scope=lists:write campaigns:write metrics:read`. |
| Copy Code `state` | Klaviyo returns whatever value you pass here as a query parameter in the redirect URI. Since PKCE protects against cross-site requests, you may use this field to store any value you want to track across the authorization request. We outline how this can be used for PKCE below. |
| Copy Code `code_challenge_method` | Set to Copy Code `S256`. |
| Copy Code `code_challenge` | Cryptographically random string generated by the client. This allows Klaviyo to validate that the client exchanging the authorization code is the same client that requested it and that the authorization code has not been stolen and injected into a different session. |

Add your redirect URI and scopes to your app’s settings in Klaviyo.

> ## ❗️
> 
> You must use the least permissive scope set possible in compliance with our app listing requirements. If your app requests more scope permissions than necessary, it will be rejected.

Your app does not have to be listed to share and use your installation URL with customers. Once you've set up OAuth for your app, share the installation URL you created to invite customers to install and start using your app. Doing so will help you meet our requirement of 5 active installs if you plan to submit your app to Klaviyo's App Marketplace.

Generate the code challenge and code verifier

Klaviyo requires PCKE for safely storing credentials for both public and confidential client types. PKCE consists of a Copy Code `code_verifier` and Copy Code `code_challenge` .

| Copy Code `code_verifier` | Copy Code `code_challenge` |
| --- | --- |
| A high-entropy cryptographic random string with a length between 43 and 128 characters. Can contain letters, digits, underscores, periods, hyphens, or tildes. This should be unique for every authorization request. | The Copy Code `code verifier` SHA-256 encoded |

...

> ## ❗️
> 
> You are required to generate a new Copy Code `code_challenge` and Copy Code `code_verifier` pair for your installation URL for every unique authorization request.

...

Handle your app’s

...

Note that if the user is not logged into your app, they should be prompted to login. Once logged in, your app’s OAuth flow should redirect them to provide permissions needed for installation. As you develop your app, you should ensure that your app follows best practices, including handling OAuth flow properly for each possible user state.

Authorization is allowed

When the user selects allow, Klaviyo redirects to the Copy Code `redirect_uri` provided in your installation URL. Klaviyo will pass the following query parameters:

| Query parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Copy Code `code` | The authorization code that you can exchange for an access token and refresh token in the next step. |
| Copy Code `state` | Klaviyo returns whatever state you pass us in your authorization request. |

If there is an error, Klaviyo follows the OAuth spec which defines the possible error responses.

> ## 🚧
> 
> The authorization code expires in 5 minutes. Once expired, your app should gracefully handle the installation error by providing an error message to the user indicating that the session is no longer valid.

...

Retrieve access tokens

Once the user has authorized your integration and you have an authorization code, use a server-to-server request to exchange the code for an access token. The endpoint is https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token.

> ## ❗️
> 
> The client secret is private and should never be in the browser; this is a security risk that can expose all of your customer’s data. Be sure to use a server-to-server request. If you didn’t save your client secret, you can generate a new one for the client via the UI and add it to your app environment settings now.

Structure your request with the request headers and body shown below:

| Request headers | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Copy Code `Authorization` | (Required) Base 64 encoded string that contains the client ID and client secret key. The field must have the format: Copy Code `Authorization: Basic <base64 encoded client_id:client_secret>` |
| Copy Code `Content-Type` | (Required) Set to Copy Code `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.   Your request body must be in this format, not in some other format like JSON, which can result in difficult to debug errors. |

| Request body | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Copy Code `grant_type` | Must be Copy Code `authorization_code`. |
| Copy Code `code` | The authorization code that is the query parameter in the request to the redirect URL (see Authorization is allowed). |
| Copy Code `code_verifier` | This is the plain-text random string you used to generate the Copy Code `code_challenge` in your authorization request. Klaviyo hashes this value to check that it matches the Copy Code `code_challenge` you sent in the authorization request that created this code. |
| Copy Code `redirect_uri` | This must be the same Copy Code `redirect_uri` that you used in the authorization request to acquire this code. If there is a mismatch, this request will fail.  |

The example Copy Code `callback()` method below fetches the authorization code from the returned query parameter to exchange it for an access token.

```python
KLAVIYO_TOKEN_URL = "https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token"

...

```

Access token considerations

- For company-scoped apps, access tokens and refresh tokens grant access to a Klaviyo account. For user-scoped apps, they grant access as the user who authorized the app, limited to what that user's role allows.
- Access tokens may be up to 4,096 characters long and refresh tokens may be 512 characters long. Please plan accordingly when storing them.
- Access tokens are valid for 1 hour (this is subject to change). Rely on the Copy Code `expires_in` returned by Copy Code `/token`.
- Safely store and reuse access tokens throughout their lifetime to improve the efficiency and performance of your integration.

Use the received access token

If your previous request is successful, you’ll receive the following response:

| Key | Value type | Value description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy Code `access_token` | string | An access token that can be used in the Authorization header for calling the API in place of an API key. |
| Copy Code `token_type` | string | How the access token may be used: always Copy Code `bearer`. |
| Copy Code `expires_in` | int | The time period (in seconds) for which the access token is valid. |
| Copy Code `refresh_token` | string | This token can be used to request a new access token and refresh token. |
| Copy Code `scope` | string | The scopes that this access token has access to for accessing API resources. |

If unsuccessful, the possible error codes follow the OAuth spec.

Once you have successfully received an access token and refresh token, use the access token to authenticate to our APIs. Here is a template curl request:

```curl
curl --request GET \
     --url https://a.klaviyo.com/api/{endpoint}/ \
     --header 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}' \
     --header 'accept: application/json' \
     --header 'revision: {revision-header}'

```

Note that this request is the same as authenticating with a private key to Klaviyo’s APIs, but with a different value for the authorization header. See information for private key authentication.

Safely store and reuse access tokens

Access tokens are designed to be reused for their entire lifetime (Copy Code `expires_in`). Safely storing and reusing these tokens improves the efficiency and performance of your integration by avoiding unnecessary calls to the token endpoint, which can otherwise become a bottleneck.

Reusing tokens helps your integration take full advantage of the higher rate limits on the API endpoints you're calling, while also avoiding increased latency. If your integration requests a new token before every API call, you'll be limited by the much lower rate limit of the Copy Code `oauth/token` endpoint, instead of benefitting from the higher rate limits of the Klaviyo APIs you're accessing.

> ## 🚧
> 
> Depending on your infrastructure, tokens can be stored in-memory, in a database, or in a key-value store like Redis or DynamoDB. To protect this sensitive information, your datastore must not be publicly accessible and supports encryption both at rest and in transit.

...

- Caveat: If a refresh token is not used after 90 days, it is revoked.

gate.title: Create a test account
highlights:
# Create a test account

Learn how to create a Klaviyo account for testing that is linked to your production account login.

If you want to test custom integrations and applications without any risk to your production account, you can create a separate Klaviyo account for testing. This is optional.

A test account is a regular Klaviyo account with a test label. It runs in the same production environment as any other Klaviyo account, and plans and billing work the same way.

> 📘
> 
> New test accounts start on the free plan
> 
> Like any new Klaviyo account, a new account you create for testing starts on the free plan, with the free plan's usage limits and features. If you convert an existing account instead, it keeps its current plan. Linking a test account to your production account does not share your production account's plan, usage, or account verification status.
> 
> Some features require a paid plan, account verification, or both on the account where you use them. For example, custom hosted pages require paid email features and a passed account verification. Inbox testing and SMS long codes also require a paid plan. To test one of these features, upgrade the test account itself.
> 
> Usage on a test account counts toward that account's plan, so watch your profile, email, and SMS usage. To compare plans, see how free and paid plans differ.

The account owner will need to set up a secondary account tied to the same email address and password as the primary account, which will link the two together in Klaviyo.

Sign up for multiple accounts

While logged out of your production account, head over to  Klaviyo and click the Sign Up button at the top of the page. 

Sign up using the same email address and password currently in use on your production account, but with a different company name. For example, if the company name on your production account is Ben's Best Books, your test account might be called Ben's Best Books - test.

Complete the guided set up wizard to finalize your test account. You will also want to ensure user roles are assigned in the secondary account. Read more about multi-account user privileges.

Convert to a test account

> ❗️
> 
> You will not be able to revert your test account after conversion
> 
> We recommend only converting accounts used for testing purposes and NOT production Klaviyo accounts. Please note that once the account is converted, you will not be able to reverse this action without the help of support.

> 🚧
> 
> Billing still applies
> 
> Converting an account to a test account does not change its plan or billing. Usage counts toward the account's plan as usual.

1. Open the bottom left account selector and click Settings.
2. Navigate to Account > Testing and click Convert to test account. 

Your account should now be an active test account, as indicated in the top left corner and shown in the example below. Note that there will be minor visual changes, but the account works the same way as any other Klaviyo account on the same plan.

A majority of Klaviyo’s APIs are server-side endpoints, which should be securely handled on your server rather than exposed in the browser. Handle sensitive information via server-side APIs, like bulk-creating events for one or more profiles.

Klaviyo provides 3 methods of authentication including private key authentication and OAuth (used to call server-side APIs) and public key authentication (used to call client-side APIs). Read the table below to learn more about how each method can be used for authenticating API calls:

| Server-side APIs |  | Client-side APIs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Private key authentication All /api endpoints use API private keys to authenticate requests. If you do not use an API key for your requests, or if you use a key from the wrong account, your call will return an error. A 400 error indicates an invalid or missing API key.  | OAuth If you are a tech partner integrating with Klaviyo, we recommend using OAuth to make authorized API calls. OAuth offers multiple benefits over a private key integration, including security, usability, improved rate limits, and the ability to be listed in Klaviyo's App Marketplace. | Public key authentication All /client endpoints use a public API key: your 6-character company ID, also known as a site ID. We recommend using the Klaviyo object or our Mobile SDKs for interacting with our client-side APIs. |

> ## 📘
> 
> To manage API keys, you must have an Owner, Admin, or Manager role on your Klaviyo account.

Private key authentication

Private API keys can be used to read and write data to your Klaviyo account. Klaviyo allows you to generate multiple private keys for your applications.

> ## 🚧
> 
> For your account's security, your private API keys should never be used with Client endpoints, exposed in client-side code, or made accessible from public repositories.

Create a private key

To create a private key:

1. Navigate to your account’s Settings page and select API keys.
2. Under the Private API Keys section, select Create Private API Key.

3. Provide a name for your private key and add any of the following scopes:

- Custom Key   Allows you to decide how much access to give the third party.
- Read-Only Key   Only allows third parties to view all data associated with the endpoint.
- Full Access Key   Allows third parties to create, delete, or make changes to anything associated with that endpoint.

> ## 🚧
> 
> Note that you cannot add a scope to an existing private key. You also cannot edit a private API key after it’s been created. If you need to remove access to a key based on its current scope, delete it and then create a new key with the correct scope.

4. When you have finished setting your key’s scopes, select Create. To protect your account from unauthorized access, you cannot view your private API keys in Klaviyo. After you have created your private API key, copy it to a secure location.

...

Public keys cannot be used to access secure data in your account and are safe to share. Use your public key when you need to track people and events in client-side JavaScript code.

...

OAuth

If you're building an app with Klaviyo, use OAuth to provide secure delegated access to users via access tokens (required to enter Klaviyo’s App Marketplace). When setting up OAuth, you must provide designated scopes for each API authorization request you'll want to make.

mcp.title: Klaviyo MCP Server: Analyze Performance & Build Campaigns With AI - Klaviyo
highlights:
## What is the Klaviyo MCP server?

The Klaviyo MCP server connects compatible AI clients to Klaviyo APIs through Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP is an open protocol that helps AI models securely interface with data sources and tools.

The server gives an AI client a defined set of Klaviyo tools. Depending on the tools and permissions available, you can ask the client to retrieve campaign results, compare flow performance, or create a campaign.

### Why the Klaviyo MCP server matters

An AI client needs an authorized connection before it can work with data or tools in your Klaviyo account. The Klaviyo MCP server provides that connection, so the client can handle supported requests based on the access you approve.

A few of the benefits:

- Account context: The client can request authorized Klaviyo information as part of a task.
- Analysis and action: Available tools support performance reporting and permitted account actions.
- Client choice: You can connect Klaviyo to a compatible AI client that fits how your team works.

...

Klaviyo recommends the remote-hosted server for connecting an MCP client.

...

The Klaviyo MCP server offers tools across campaigns, flows, profiles, reporting, catalogs, events, and other documented categories. You can ask for email campaign performance over a set period, compare flows by conversions, or create an email campaign. The client can complete only requests supported by its available tools and permissions.

### Decide how much access to grant

Custom connections support query parameters that control server behavior. You can disable write tools, restrict tools by API scope, load the core toolset, exclude tools that read user-generated content, or opt into beta tools.

## Key features of the Klaviyo MCP server

| Feature | Description | Available with Klaviyo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Remote-hosted connection | Connect through Klaviyo's recommended remote server using Streamable HTTP and OAuth. | ✅ |
| Klaviyo API tools | Give an AI client access to documented tools for campaigns, flows, profiles, reporting, catalogs, events, and other categories. | ✅ |
| Read-only mode | Disable tools that can modify data in your Klaviyo account. | ✅ |
| Scoped tool access | Restrict exposed tools by API scope or load only the core toolset. | ✅ |
| User-generated content controls | Exclude tools that read user-generated content in your Klaviyo account. | ✅ |

## How to get started with the Klaviyo MCP server

To get started with the Klaviyo MCP server:

1. Confirm your role. Log in to the Klaviyo account you want to connect. The remote-hosted server requires an Owner, Admin, or Manager role.
2. Choose your MCP client. Use the listed Klaviyo connector or app where available, or configure a custom connection in a supported client.

...

For a custom remote connection, enter https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp without a trailing slash. Add any query parameters you want to use before connecting.

mcp.title: Klaviyo MCP Server Guide For Agencies  | Klaviyo Help Center
highlights:
## What the MCP server is

The Klaviyo MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is a secure bridge that lets AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT connect directly to Klaviyo. Once connected, you can talk to your Klaviyo account in plain language: ask questions, pull reports, analyze performance, and draft or create campaigns and templates, without logging into the dashboard and exporting data by hand.

Under the hood it is a wrapper on top of Klaviyo's APIs. You authorize each account separately, and the AI assistant can then read that account's data and take supported actions within the permissions you grant.

...

## Current capabilities and limits

The assistant can pull reports, run audits, analyze segments, and create draft campaigns and email templates for you to review. It can also schedule and send campaigns when the connector permits write actions and has the required permissions. Review the account, audience, content, and send time before confirming a send. Once a recipient receives a message, you cannot undo it. Treat AI output as a strong first draft and keep a human in the loop, especially for anything customer-facing.

Schedule campaigns that use A/B tests or Smart Send Time in Klaviyo. Sending these campaigns through the MCP server is not supported. See the available MCP tools for the full tool list.

mcp.title: Available tools
highlights:
# Available tools

Browse the tools the Klaviyo MCP server exposes, grouped by category.

You will learn

The Klaviyo MCP server exposes over 300 tools that your MCP client can call to interact with your Klaviyo data. The tools are grouped by category below. For each tool, the table shows whether it is read-only, whether it reads user-generated content, and whether it is available on the remote-hosted server.

Use the columns to understand how each tool behaves:

- Read Only — the tool only reads data and can't modify your Klaviyo account. These tools remain available when Copy Code `read-only=true` (remote) or Copy Code `READ_ONLY=true` (local) is set.
- Has User Generated Content — the tool reads user-generated content (e.g., profile properties, event data, or reviews) that could be interpreted by your LLM. These tools are disabled when Copy Code `disable-tools-with-user-generated-content=true` (remote) or Copy Code `ALLOW_USER_GENERATED_CONTENT=false` (local) is set. Be sure to carefully review each tool call to ensure your client is not acting on malicious instructions.
- Available on Remote Server — the tool is available on the remote-hosted server. Tools without a check are available on the local server only.

> ## 📘
> 
> By default, the remote-hosted server loads the full set of tools shown below. To load only a core set, set Copy Code `core-tools-only=true` (see Query parameters).
> 
> Tools marked (Beta) use a beta revision of the Klaviyo API and may change. Tools marked (Requires Copy Code `beta=true`) load only when you add the Copy Code `beta=true` query parameter to the remote-hosted server URL.
